claims.claim: The checked native Blackwell backend boundary is between Triton v3.2.0 and v3.3.0: the corresponding TCGen5/TMEM/MMAv5 symbols are absent at the former tag, while the latter contains operations, allocation/lowering passes, and conversion tests for concrete output.

evidence.locator: TCGen5MMA, TCGen5MMAScaled, and TMEM operation definitions
evidence.observation: The tagged dialect defines native TCGen5 MMA/scaled-MMA and tensor-memory operations.

evidence.locator: FileCheck expectations for tcgen05 MMA, commit, TMEM, scaled MMA, and cta_group::2
evidence.observation: The conversion suite requires concrete Blackwell-native output rather than merely declaring unused operations.

evidence.locator: TritonNvidiaGPU operations, MMAv5 lowering, tensor-memory allocation, and Blackwell tests
evidence.observation: The corresponding backend enters in this tag interval; exact-tree search finds no matching backend symbols at v3.2.0.

challenge.alternative: The v3.3 operations are unused scaffolding, and native lowering actually begins in v3.6.
challenge.check: Compare the exact v3.2 and v3.3 trees and inspect the v3.3 conversion test expectations.
challenge.outcome: The earlier tree lacks the backend symbols and the v3.3 tests require concrete TCGen5/TMEM output, discriminating real lowering from scaffolding.

claims.claim: By v3.5.0 Triton ships explicit Gluon TCGen5/TMEM and Blackwell block-scaled matmul tutorials; v3.6.0 incrementally broadens layouts, copies, warp specialization, and initial multi-CTA/2-CTA Gluon support, while v3.7.0 continues 2-CTA/multicast/TMA work and v3.7.1 is a regression-only patch.

evidence.observation: The pinned tutorial allocates, loads, and stores TMEM and invokes TCGen5 MMA through Gluon.
The v3.5 tag already contains the tl.dot_scaled Blackwell tutorial.

evidence.locator: Blackwell, TMEM, tcgen05, warp-specialization, and Gluon release-note entries
evidence.observation: The release enumerates generalization and initial multi-CTA/2-CTA work on top of earlier capabilities.
The next minor release contains further end-to-end Blackwell cluster-path work.
The patch release lists two regression fixes and explicitly advertises no new API or feature.

challenge.alternative: The tutorials and native surfaces first appear only in v3.6, and v3.7.1 adds another feature milestone.
challenge.check: Open both tutorials at the exact v3.5 tag and compare the v3.6, v3.7, and v3.7.1 release descriptions.
challenge.outcome: The tutorials exist at v3.5, the v3.6/v3.7 notes describe successive expansions, and v3.7.1 describes only regression fixes.

claims.claim: vLLM PR 34597 adds FP8 KV-cache handling to a Triton MLA decode backend whose pinned kernel contains the displayed verbatim FP8-rescaling/tl.dot excerpt; the PR names SM120, while neither the PR nor code proves an SM100-only path or a particular TCGen5/TMEM lowering.

evidence.observation: The PR adds FP8 cache support and identifies the Triton backend as the MLA option on SM120; it makes no SM100-only or instruction-lowering claim.

evidence.locator: kernel definitions and tl.dot call sites
evidence.observation: The code contains Triton JIT kernels and tl.dot but no architecture guard, Triton-version requirement, warp_specialize, TCGen5/TMEM name, or emitted PTX.

challenge.alternative: The local architecture field or the presence of tl.dot is enough to demonstrate SM100 TCGen5 emission.
challenge.check: Inspect the primary PR motivation, exact code guards, and any emitted-IR/PTX evidence.
challenge.outcome: The primary source names SM120 and supplies no target guard or lowering witness, so the page retains only the narrower implementation claim.

claims.claim: On 2026-08-08 the live FlashInfer-Bench author leaderboard shows 0.628x/73.1% for Gemini 2.5 Pro, 0.467x/92.3% for GPT-5, and 0.456x/73.1% for Claude Opus 4.1, each across 660 workloads; it gives no Triton-release or Triton-only scope for those rows.

evidence.locator: Author / Avg Speedup / % Resolved rows for the three named authors
evidence.observation: The exact values and 660-workload denominators appear in the labeled rows; the page exposes no Triton version or Triton-only filter.

challenge.alternative: The values are historical Triton 3.5 results or belong to adjacent model/workload columns.
challenge.check: Read each author row under the labeled columns and inspect the page for version and language metadata.
challenge.outcome: The values map directly to the author rows, and no claimed Triton version/language scope is present.

claims.claim: SGLang PR 5390 reports a scoped 10,447.34-versus-8,227.35 total-token-throughput comparison (26.98%), and PR 21595 changes the SM100 datacenter multimodal-attention default from triton_attn to FA4.

evidence.locator: DeepSeek-R1 benchmark commands and CUTLASS/Triton result blocks
evidence.observation: The PR records the two totals and the stated 3,000-prompt, TP8/DP8, float16, 1,000-input/1,000-output-token scope.
The PR explicitly scopes the default switch to Blackwell SM100 datacenter multimodal attention.

challenge.alternative: The percentage compares different metrics, or the routing change applies to every GPU and workload.
challenge.check: Use the total-token-throughput field in both PR 5390 result blocks and the architecture condition in PR 21595.
challenge.outcome: The quotient is 26.98%, and the routing change is explicitly SM100-scoped.

claims.claim: The page's triton-universe link resolves to the canonical ledger containing the tracked PR entries and their captured flags without duplicating its mutable count.

evidence.reference: The relative link must resolve and the YAML must expose a PR collection with per-entry captured flags.
evidence.result: The link resolves; the canonical YAML parses with 267 PR entries, each carrying a captured flag, while the wiki text states no copied count.

challenge.alternative: The link points to a stale summary or the target lacks capture status.
challenge.check: Resolve the exact relative path and inspect every PR entry for the captured key, alongside a broken-target control.
challenge.outcome: The exact canonical target resolves and all entries expose the flag; the negative control fails.

claims.claim: vLLM PR 29339 is an SM90/SM100 MXFP4 triton_kernels dispatch gate rather than a new Triton kernel or compiler-lowering implementation.

evidence.observation: The PR gates triton_kernels MXFP4 use to SM90 and SM100 and does not add a Triton kernel.

challenge.alternative: The PR adds a target-specific Triton kernel or demonstrates a TCGen5 lowering.
challenge.check: Inspect the exact one-file diff and changed-files list.
challenge.outcome: Only dispatch logic changes; no Triton kernel, IR, or PTX is added.

claims.claim: SGLang PR 21019 is a load/store GatedDeltaNet projection rearrangement without tl.dot, while PR 22079 is extend-attention code with tl.dot but no emitted-PTX witness.

evidence.locator: Triton kernel load/store sites and whole-file tl.dot search
evidence.observation: The verbatim kernel rearranges projection data with loads/stores and contains no tl.dot.

evidence.locator: Triton extend-attention kernels and tl.dot sites
evidence.observation: The verbatim code contains QK and probability/value dot products but no TCGen5 PTX dump.

challenge.alternative: The page swaps which SGLang artifact contains matrix products or either file contains an emitted TCGen5 witness.
challenge.check: Inspect each exact file for decorators, tl.dot, load/store operations, TCGen5 names, and PTX.
challenge.outcome: The GDN file is a load/store rearrangement, the attention file contains the dot products, and neither provides emitted TCGen5 PTX.

claims.claim: CUDA Graphs reduce repeated CPU launch costs for short-kernel workflows; at vLLM commit a1257fd1 the v1 default is FULL_AND_PIECEWISE and the GatedDeltaNet backend supports uniform-batch graphs and decode full capture.

evidence.observation: The guide identifies host setup as significant for short kernels and explains that graphs reduce CPU launch costs by preparing work in advance.
FULL_AND_PIECEWISE is documented as the v1 default.
The GDN backend advertises uniform-batch graph support and implements decode-only full graph capture.

challenge.alternative: Graphs do not address CPU launch cost, or GatedDeltaNet opts out of vLLM's graph path.
challenge.check: Inspect the CUDA guide and the exact vLLM compilation default and GDN metadata builder.
challenge.outcome: The primary documentation connects graphs to launch cost, and the pinned backend explicitly implements the capture path.

claims.claim: The checked compiler sources prove native TCGen5/TMEM paths exist, but the cited downstream kernels do not prove exact instruction selection for arbitrary tl.dot shapes.

evidence.environment: GNU ripgrep over provenance-pinned downstream artifacts
evidence.reference: An explicit lowering witness would name the backend mechanism or include emitted IR/PTX; a known upstream positive control must match the same search.
evidence.result: No explicit lowering witness occurs in the three downstream bundles.
evidence.negative_control: The identical terms match the pinned Triton v3.5.0 TCGen5 tutorial and the v3.3.0 compiler/test sources.

challenge.alternative: Every tl.dot in a post-boundary downstream kernel necessarily demonstrates TCGen5 emission.
challenge.check: Search exact downstream source for target guards, backend names, IR, or PTX and compare to a known matching upstream control.
challenge.outcome: The downstream files contain none of the discriminating witnesses while the controls do, so the page does not infer an unobserved lowering.
